data.reason: Nothing has been produced and the ladder still requires technical_spec, dev_plan, capability and implementation. The technical spec comes first because the other artifacts depend on the decisions it fixes.
data.wave_reason: Only the technical spec is produced now. The dev plan, the capability and the implementation each need the behaviour and structure decisions the spec fixes, and agents in the same wave cannot see each other's output. Capability criteria written in parallel could contradict the spec on the open edge cases (P before the first key, P on an end screen, which key restarts). Six waves remain, so serialising costs nothing.

gap.statement: There is no technical spec for pause/resume on P and the end-of-game score screen. Without it, the game-loop and state changes, and the choices the intent leaves open, are undecided. Those choices decide what a test can check and what code gets written.

premises.text: The intent asks for a P-key pause/resume that freezes pacman and the ghosts with no eating and no losing while paused. It also asks for a final score drawn on the canvas at win or loss, shown until a key restarts the game. It leaves open how pause interacts with the not-yet-started state, the end screens, and the restart key.
The ladder for this brownfield, prototype-rigor plan marks technical_spec as required and missing, and nothing has been produced yet.

blocks: dev_plan (needs the parts and flows to sequence)
capability (needs the settled pause and end-screen behaviour to state testable criteria)
implementation (needs the approach and state model)

artifacts.task: Write the technical spec for the pause and end-of-game score feature against the existing game code. Cover the game state to add (paused flag, ended state with won or lost and final score); the game-loop changes that freeze pacman and ghost movement, eating and life loss while paused; the P key handling; the score screen drawn on the canvas until a key restarts the game; and the restart path. Decide the edge cases the intent leaves open: P before the first key, P on an end screen, which key restarts and whether it also starts play, and key input while paused. Say how it is tested, and keep it prototype-sized.

rejected.why: Its criteria depend on edge-case decisions (P before start, P on end screens, restart key) that the spec should fix first. Written in parallel by an agent that cannot see the spec, it could contradict it.
It sequences work over parts and flows the spec defines, and the spec does not exist yet.
Code without a spec or a contract would leave the ambiguous behaviours to be settled implicitly.
The intent is already a small, concrete feature request. The ladder does not require a brief, and it would add no decision the spec does not.
The ladder still requires four artifacts the catalogue can produce, so a no-move would be refused.
